question:
A p–n junction diode has a built-in potential $V_{bi}=0.75\,\text{V}$ at $300\,\text{K}$. The depletion width at zero bias is measured as $W_0=0.60\,\mu\text{m}$.

Assume an abrupt junction where depletion width varies with effective barrier as</br>

 $W \propto \sqrt{V_{\text{barrier}}}.$ 

(a) Under a reverse bias of $V_R=4.0\,\text{V}$, calculate the new depletion width $W_R$ using the scaling</br>

 $\frac{W_R}{W_0}=\sqrt{\frac{V_{bi}+V_R}{V_{bi}}}.$ 

(b) Under a forward bias of $V_F=0.30\,\text{V}$, calculate the new depletion width $W_F$ using the scaling</br>

 $\frac{W_F}{W_0}=\sqrt{\frac{V_{bi}-V_F}{V_{bi}}}.$ 

(c) A student claims: “Reverse bias reduces the barrier potential, hence it narrows the depletion region and increases diffusion current.” Evaluate this claim using your results and correct physical reasoning.

(d) Draw two qualitative diagrams of the junction showing how the depletion region and barrier change in (i) forward bias and (ii) reverse bias.

(e) Draw a qualitative $I$–$V$ curve of a diode and mark the regions of forward conduction and reverse saturation current, relating each region to depletion width change.

options.A: $W_R\approx 1.51\,\mu\text{m}$ and $W_F\approx 0.47\,\mu\text{m}$; reverse bias increases barrier and widens depletion region, reducing majority diffusion; the student’s claim is incorrect; diagrams and $I$–$V$ curve consistent.
options.B: $W_R\approx 0.24\,\mu\text{m}$ and $W_F\approx 1.20\,\mu\text{m}$; reverse bias reduces barrier and narrows depletion; the student’s claim is correct.
options.C: $W_R\approx 0.60\,\mu\text{m}$ and $W_F\approx 0.60\,\mu\text{m}$; depletion width is independent of bias; the student’s claim is irrelevant.
options.D: $W_R\approx 1.51\,\mu\text{m}$ and $W_F\approx 0.47\,\mu\text{m}$; but reverse bias decreases barrier while still widening depletion; the student’s claim is correct.
